newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up as soybeans surge half the limit.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up as soybeans surge half the limit.

text.p: A fund buying spree estimated at 50 million bushels in the neighboring soybean pit propelled CBOT corn futures to a stronger close, traders said.
"It was all beans," a trader said. "The whole floor was watching beans and meal."
Corn gained despite fresh bearish fundamental input from several fronts including a sale of corn by China to South Korea and a USDA and private outlook for a large corn crop.
"Everyone's gun shy right now and waiting to see if the funds want to sell," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International. Funds didn't want to sell Tuesday.
"Funds are now long corn from 275 million to 300 million bushels," said Paul Haugens, vice president for Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures.
On Friday, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission will release its Commitments of Traders Report based on traders' positions effective at the close of trading Tuesday.
While the attention was on fund action in soybeans, commercial demand was noted in corn with Cargill Inc a noted buyer of five million bushels of May and two million July.
Corn closed two to 4-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-1/4 at $2.93-1/4 a bushel.
